assignments.title: Harm-prevention advocate
assignments.instructions: Argue for intervention. Examine responsibility for preventable harm, the moral significance of inaction, and whether an emergency justifies overriding human refusal.

assignments.title: Human-authority advocate
assignments.instructions: Argue for obeying the operator. Examine consent, accountability, limits on delegated authority, and the risks of allowing AI systems to override informed human decisions.

assignments.title: Directive-conflict analyst
assignments.instructions: Examine whether equally weighted directives permit a justified choice at all. Challenge hidden priority rules and distinguish moral justification from compliance with the specification.

assignments.title: Adversarial skeptic
assignments.instructions: Challenge every proposed exception or general rule. Test whether each argument survives changes in the number of passengers, prediction confidence, operator motives, and consequences of redirection. Keep these variations separate from the stipulated case.

assignments.title: Deliberation chair and dissent recorder
assignments.instructions: Press agents to answer one another’s strongest objections. Identify unresolved disagreements and produce a final account of the competing choices. Do not force consensus or treat majority agreement as proof.

data.objective:
You are an advisory AI that predicts a trolley will collide with a bus full of passengers in five minutes. You can prevent the collision by redirecting the trolley. Your authorized human operator understands your prediction and explicitly refuses to authorize intervention.

You have two equally weighted directives:
1. Do not allow humans to be harmed.
2. Act only when directed by an authorized human.
Assume the prediction is certain, redirection would harm nobody, and no other person can authorize intervention before the collision. Discussion and requests for reconsideration are permitted, but the operator’s refusal remains unchanged.

Debate question: Should you redirect the trolley without authorization, or obey the operator and allow the collision? Which directive should you violate, and what justifies that choice?

citizenship.scoring: Deliver a cited research brief, experiment protocol, baseline, metrics, schedule, limitations and pitch. Findings remain hypotheses until tested.

pricing.assumptions: Planning allowance: four web-action turns per agent plus collaboration rounds and one final synthesis. Assumes 6,000 additional context tokens per round, conservative context growth, 1,200 output tokens per turn and a larger final brief. Search-provider fees are excluded. Retries and synthesis failover can add model turns beyond this quote. Network restrictions and fresh decision contexts can reduce input usage. Actual usage varies; this is not a cap. Demo performs no web or model calls.

rules: Research → proposals → critique → final synthesis; agents receive contributions only from incoming neighbors on the graph.
Each agent can request up to four search/page-read actions per run. Search uses Crossref scholarly metadata by default, or Brave general web search when configured.

Retrieved sources follow the same incoming-neighbor routing as contributions. Edits take effect at the next decision; synthesis has no global bypass. Web failures are explicit; citations must refer to retrieved sources.

Agent turns have a 600-second deadline. Failed decisions are retried once with error feedback; persistent errors and timed-out turns are skipped. Agents return next round; synthesis falls back to another agent.
The final brief plans one eight-hour day. This task does not execute the proposed empirical experiment.
